Mr. Md. Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury, Senior Advocate with Mr. Mohammad Shafikul Islam Ripon, Advocates ------ For the petitioners. 
Mr. Md. Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan, Advocate ------ For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Md. Rafique and Others
Vs.
Sayed Md. Abdul Quiyum being dead his heirs: Mst. Rokeya khatun and others
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.11.2014 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.19 of 2013 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.01.2013 and 20.01.2013 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka in Title Suit No.34 of 2011 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original title suit being No.34 of 2011 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka for declaration of title along with a prayer for cancellation of a deed and perpetual injunction contending inter alia, that the disputed property appertaining to Mouza Khilgaon in C.S. Plot No.10P was the property under the government as abandoned property and the government decided to settle the land in favour of private individual. Accordingly, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff Fakir Chand pursuant to his prayer for taking permanent settlement was obtained allotment of the suit properties which was in fact initially acquired by the government in L.A. Case No.47 of 1959-60 and 11 of 1960-61. The predecessor of the plaintiff Fakir Chand obtained allotment on 02.11.1961 in respect of 02(two) kathas 07(seven) chhatak land of plot No. A-627(F) and 628(P) from the office of the concerned Executive Engineer, Public Works Department (PWD) followed by an allotment latter being Memo No.8059 (RDD) dated 02.11.1961. That the possession was delivered in favour of allotment-holder on 08.11.1965. Fakir Chand under the terms and conditions of the latter of allotment for obtaining a lease deed erected a tin-shed but on the suit property in the year 1965 and used to possess that homestead as of his dwelling hut. The further case of the plaintiff is such that Fakir Chand possessed the property through his caretaker and expired before 24/25 years. At his death; his two sons the plaintiff No. l and 2 one daughter, the plaintiff No.3 and one wife the plaintiff No.4 and mother of plaintiff No. 5 and 6 Halima Khatun became the heirs. The father of the plaintiff No.5 and 6 namely Rustom Ali as caretaker of the property used to look after the property. Rustom Ali while became bed ridden due to his paralysis disease, his wife Halima Khatun along with other plaintiffs use to possess the same in ejmali. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that the father of the defendants No.1-4 Altaf Hossain who was very much familiar to Rustom Ali Khan was allowed to possess the suit property without rent after the death of Altaf Hossain. The defendants No.1-4 concealed the original papers of the plaintiff. The government on 25.02.1982 executed and registered a lease deed being No.4643 in the name of Fakir Chand when Fakir Chand was already expired. The plaintiffs requested the government officials to register the lease deed in favour of them; but the office of the defendant No.7 disclosed before them that the lease deed has already been executed and registered in favour of their predecessor Fakir Chand. On 07.03.2010 the plaintiffs finding a sign board in the name of the defendant No.5 in the suit property they inquired into the matter and came to learn that the mother of the defendants No.1-4 Umme Salma Akter Khatun as am-mokter of Fakir Chand transferred the suit property on 10.09.1995 in favour of the defendants No.1-4 by a transfer deed No. 5278. The defendants No.1-4 entered into a contract with the defendant No.5 to construct a multistoried building in the suit property and according to that contract; the defendant No.5 hanged a signboard, which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendants in short is thus that Fakir Chand obtained the allotment of the suit property by an allotment letter No.8059 dated 02.11.1961 from the government. Possession was delivered in favour of the lease-holder on 08.11.1965. Subsequently; Fakir Chand transferred the suit property in favour of the father of the defendants No.1-4 on 10.11.1970. For execution and registration of the sale deed both Fakir Chand and Altaf Hossain entered into a deed of agreement on 12.01.1970. The consideration money was fixed at Taka 15,000/-. On the date of deed of agreement Fakir Chand after taking a sum of Taka 13,500/- from Altaf Hossain handed over possession of the property. On the same date Fakir Chand executed a power of attorney on his behalf in the name of the wife of Altaf Hossain namely Umme Salina Khatun in respect of the disputed property and it was clearly mentioned in the power of attorney that Fakir Chand entered into a deed of agreement to sale the property in favour of Altaf Hossain and his attorney is empowered to execute and register the sale deed in favour of Altaf Hossain. The further case of the defendants is such that Fakir Chand since 12.01.1970 never looked after the property and his attorney Umme Salina Akter used to manage everything on his behalf and accordingly the government of Bangladesh recognizing the attorney Salma Akter registered the lease deed No.4643 on 25.02.1982 A.D. and in the lease deed the signature of attorney Umme Salina Khatun was obtained. It was further case of the defendants that their father Altaf Hossain in the year 1981 died leaving behind his legal heirs. After the death of Altaf Hossain by amicable partition the defendants No.1-4 use to possess the suit property and accordingly the attorney Salina Khatun for want of making a registered sale deed in favour of the defendants No.1-4 filed an application to the concerned Ministry of Housing and Public Works. Accordingly, the concerned Ministry pursuant to their memo No. 6/L-95/2107/1(2) dated 08.08.1995 gave permission to the attorney Salma Khatun for transfer of the property in favour of the defendants No.1-4. Thereafter, Salina Akter Khatun transferred the suit land in favour of the defendants No.1- 4 by a registered sub-kabala No. 5278 dated 10.09.1995. The defendants No.1-4 subsequently mutated their names and paying rent regularly. During city survey the suit land has been properly recorded in the names of the defendants No.1-4 and the defendant-opposite parties No.1-4 are paying upto date gas bill, city corporation holding tax, electricity bill etc. Recently they have decided to construct a multistoried building in the suit property and for that necessity they made a contract with the defendant No.5 a developer company to contract a multistoried building therein and the developer company according to their construct have prepared to construct the same. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiffs having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the suit property on the basis of false allegations filed the suit, which is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after examining 07 witnesses from the side of the plaintiffs and 03 witnesses from the side of the defendants evaluating the documentary and oral evidence produced from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 13.01.2013. 

 5. Being aggrieved the plaintiff preferred a title appeal being No.19 of 2013 in the court of learned District Jude, Dhaka which was transmitted to the 2nd Court of learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka for hearing and disposal and the learned Additional District Judge by the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.11.2014 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and dismissal decree passed by the trial court. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned trial court as well as the lower appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that admittedly after the death of Fakir Chand the lease deed in the name of Fakir Chand was executed and registered by the admitted owner of the property; government of Bangladesh and on the basis of agreement for sale before the lease deed the defendants have claimed the property from their vendor the alleged power of attorney of Fakir Chand Umme Salma Khatun, but in fact; there is no legal basis to transfer the property in favour of anybody prior to the lease deed executed and registered by the government. The learned Advocate further submits that the papers in favour of the defendants are collusive and forged having no legal basis which is totally ignored by both the courts below. The learned Advocate also submits that the courts below erred in law in disbelieving the evidence of the plaintiff's witnesses without any cogent reason as to the death of Fakir Chand. The learned appellate court below during deciding the fate of the appeal failed to assess the evidence on record in its true perspective and arrived at an erroneous decision that the plaintiffs to the suit failed to discharge their onus of proof by any trust worthy evidence while the defendants to the suit in respect of their respective case successfully proved that they have acquired right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. The learned Advocate argued that the positive contention as transpired from the pleading of the plaintiffs was not considered by the courts below during passing their judgment and decree, which is an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate in support of his argument referred some decisions of this Court and our Apex Court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the basic documents of the defendants were not properly evaluated by the learned courts below in their observation and findings. Under the ambit of Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure there has been material omission with regard to the materials on record and there is a misreading and non-reading of evidence as well as non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning of failure of justice, which deserve interference of this Court. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioners and submits that there is no illegality or irregularity from the sides of the learned trial court as well as from the side of the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned appellate court below during disposal of the appeal rightly assessed the evidence on record in its true perspective and there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and both the courts below concurrently held on proper evaluation of the evidence on records that the plaintiffs to the suit have measurably failed to discharge their onus of proof and on the contrary the defendants by adducing sufficient tangible evidence from their side successfully proved their specific case as agitated within their pleading in their written statement. The learned Advocate also submits that the admitted owner of the property government' by their execution and registration of the lease deed in favour of Fakir Chand completed the process of their allotment in favour of allottee of the suit property, Fakir Chand and the entire proceedings of the allotment was ended by execution and registration of the deed of lease and the lease-holder Fakir Chand legally acquired his right to property in the suit holding and also obtained the possession therein. Both the courts below concurrently observed in their findings and decision that the documentary evidence produced from the side of the defendants makes it clear that the title of the property was properly acquired by the defendants and the series of papers goes to show that in the disputed property; the contesting defendants No.1-4 acquired their right, title, interest and possession which is admitted practically from the admission of the plaintiff ~s witnesses during their depositions before the trial Court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the witnesses of the plaintiffs in fact proved the case of the defendants as a whole; and it is not the case of the plaintiff-petitioners that the witnesses have become hostile or biased in favour of the defendants. The official witnesses produced from the side of the plaintiffs also have totally proved the case of the defendants in toto in their testimonies which are already on records and properly evaluated by the learned courts below in their observation and findings and there is nothing on record to show that the trial court as well as the appellate court committed any wrong or illegality during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal. The learned Advocate in support of his contention referred some decisions of our Apex Court and lastly concluded his submissions stating that the civil Rule having no merit is liable to be discharged. 

 10. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates I have gone through the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate court in Title Appeal No.19 of 2013 and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Title Suit No.34 of 2011 along with the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties; both oral and documentary. I have also perused the connected papers including the original plaint of the plaintiffs and the written statement submitted from the side of the contesting defendants. 

 11. On perusal of the case records it transpires that admittedly the disputed property was the property of the government which was acquired by them pursuant to Land Acquisition Case No.47 of 1959-60 and 11 of 1960-61. It is also an admitted position that Fakir Chand as a deserving person prayed for taking lease of the property and the authority concerned being pleased gave him allotment letter followed by a Office Memo No.8059(RDD) dated 02.11.1961 in respect of the suit land measuring 02 kathas 07 chhatak. It is also an admitted position that the concerned department of the government i.e. Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Dhaka after their allotment letter handed over possession of the property in favour of Fakir Chand. The allotment-holder thereafter in the year 1965 erected a tinshed but in the suit property and started to reside therein. It is the case of the plaintiffs in their plaint that their predecessor-in-interest Fakir Chand died on 08.09.1981. But the fact remains that the lease deed was registered on 25.02.1982 wherein there is a signature of the Attorney of Fakir Chand Umme namely Salma Khatun and it is the specific case of the defendants that Fakir Chand during his life time for want of disposal of the property in favour of Altaf Hossain, the father of the defendants No.1-4 entered into a deed of agreement on 12.01.1970 and in the deed of agreement which was a registered instrument, the consideration amount was fixed at Tk.15,000/-; out of which on the date of agreement Altaf Hossain paid Tk.13,500/- in favour of Fakir Chand. The possession was delivered on the same date in favour of Altaf Hossain. It is found that the attorney Umme Salina Khatun who happens to be mother of the defendants No.1-4 and wife of Altaf Hossain was appointed the attorney by Fakir Chand on 12.01.1970 by virtue of a registered power of attorney in respect of disputed property and by dint of that power (authority) Umme Salma Khatun as attorney put her signature in the registered lease deed No. 4643 dated 25.02.1982. 

 12. Consulting the connected papers meticulously it further transpires that the attorney was entrusted to dispose of the property followed by the transfer deed in favour of Altaf Hossain, the father of the defendants and at his demise, the defendants No.1-4 along with his other  brothers and sisters became the heirs who amicably started to possess the property left behind Altaf Hossain and the suit property by that amicable partition was under the possession of the defendants No.1-4. The attorney Umme Salina Khatun decided to transfer the suit land in favour of the possession-holders defendants No.1-4 and for the legal necessity to execute and register the transfer deeds he filed an application to the government. On behalf of the government the Ministry of Housing and public Works pursuant to their office Memo No.6/L-95/2107/1(2) dated 08.08.1995 gave a permission in writing to the attorney of Fakir Chand, Umme Salma Khatun to transfer the property in favour of the defendant-opposite parties and accordingly after getting permission from the government; the attorney by a registered sub-kabala deed dated 10.09.1995 transferred the suit land in favour of the defendant-opposite parties No.1-4. It further transpires from the papers on records and the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties that the purchaser-defendants No.1-4 after mutating their names in the government sheresta regularly paying rent for the suit property and getting rent receipts. It also appears from the papers on records that in respect of the disputed property there is a holding number of City Corporation and there is a payment of Gas bill, Electricity bill etc. in the name of Altaf Hossain who is admittedly the father of the defendants No.1-4. 

 13. Having gone through the records 1 find that, both the parties to substantiate their case have adduced witnesses. P.W.1; the plaintiff No.4 Md. Solid Khan who has deposed on behalf of the plaintiffs No.1-4 and 6 as of their Attorney. This witness in his testimony testified at a stage of his examination-in-chief that on 08.09.1981 Fakir Chand who was their father died. This witness also testified at a stage of his deposition that their father for want of execution of a deed in favour of the predecessor father of the defendants No.1-4, Altaf Hossain in respect of the disputed property handed over all the original papers in favour of Altaf Hossain and after the death of Altaf Hossain the defendants did not hand over those papers to them (the plaintiffs). It was also testified by this plaintiff No.04 that their father paid all the dues in favour of the government. P.W.1 identified the lease deed No.4643 dated 25.02.1982. He further testified that on 07.03.2007 he found a sign board in the name of a developer company in the suit property. During his deposition P.W. 1 frankly conceded that the defendants applied for a plan to D.I.T. and also testified that the original lease deed, letter of allotment and original copies of chalan in respect of the disputed property lies in favour of the predecessor of the defendants, Altaf Hossain. In a reply to a question during his cross-examination from the side of the defendants, P.W.1 testified at a stage that Umme Salma filed an application to dispose of the property in favour of the defendants No.1-4 in the concerned Ministry of Housing and Public Works of the government and obtained permission from the government to dispose of the property in favour of the defendants No.1-4. It is also admitted from the side of the plaintiff No.4 that the predecessor of the defendant-opposite parties, Altaf Hossain used to reside in the suit property. As to the death of Fakir Chand P.W.1 in his cross-examination testified that on 08.09.1989 Fakir Chand died. Subsequently; the same witness, plaintiff No.4 stated that Fakir Chand in the year 1981 expired. He has conceded during his cross-examination from the side of the defendants that in the lease deed on behalf of Fakir Chand his attorney Umme Salina Akter put her signature. He has admitted in his testimony during his cross-examination that in the death certificate issued by the City Corporation; which was produced from their side, there is a recital to the effect that Fakir Chand died on 05.09.2007 and there is no paper showing their mutation, payment of rent, payment of gas bill, water bill and electricity bill in respect of the suit property and they have failed to produce any scrap of paper to that effect. P.W.1 at a stage of his cross-examination in reply to a question from the side of the defendants admits that in the deed of agreement dated 12.01.1970 being No.370 there is a signature of his grandmother Fakir Chand and in every page of this "bainanama" the name of Fakir Chand is visible. 

 14. The witness No.2 of the plaintiff Md. Abdul Halim in his testimony testified that, he knows the parties and the suit property and he also knew Fakir Chanel. In the testimony P.W.2 testified at a stage that in the suit property the defendants use to reside and the mother of the defendants, Umme Salina along with her husband Altai Hossain in what basis started to reside in the disputed property-it is not known to him (P.W.2). He also does not know as to whether Fakir Chand on 12.01.1970 appointed Umme Salina Akter his attorney. This witness admits that Umme Salma died in the suit property. 

 16. P.W.4 Abu Siddique in his deposition testified at a stage that he does not know the suit land. 

 17. P.W.5 Md. Fazal Hossain in his testimony testified at a stage that, perhaps the suit property has been allotted in favour of Fakir Chand and at that time he was a minor boy of 05 years. 

 18. P.W.6 Md. Hasan Ali, who is a man of different area; testified at a stage that lie does not know as to whether Fakir Chand was the owner of the suit property and it is also not known to him that, as to whether Fakir Chand entered into a deed of agreement with Altaf Hossain or appointed Salma Akter as of his attorney through a power of attorney. 

 20. Vis-a-vis; the defendant's witness D.W.1 is the defendant No.1(Ka) Mst. Rokeya Khatun. This witness corroborated the case of their written statement in her deposition. She has also testified about their title documents which are on records and possession in favour of them. 

 21. D.w.2 Md. Rafique Ulla testified about the possession of Altai Hossain in the suit property through him who was a tenant under Altaf Hossain. He has corroborated the defendant's case in his testimony. 

 22. The last witness of' the defendant's, D.W.3 Md. Abul Kashem Akon testified about the case of the defendants as to their right, title, interest and possession in the disputed property. All the D.W.s have been thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the plaintiffs but except some minor discrepancies no such material contradiction or omission is noticed in their testimony by which they can be disbelieved. 

 24. Going through the evidence on records and connected all other papers it is obvious to note that, the learned courts below in their observation and findings evaluated the evidence on records in its true perspective and after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law rightly and legally decided the merit of the suit and its subsequent appeal against the plaintiffs and in favour of the defendants. I find no such misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. It further appears from the impugned judgment and decree that the learned appellate court under the ambit of Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure on preponderance of evidence arrived at a conclusive decision as to the right, title, interest and possession of' the parties to the suit and in the observation and findings as it appears, there is no ambiguity or illegality by which it can be held that the judgment and decree is perverse. 

 26. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 25.11.2014 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.19 of 2013 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.01.2013 and 20.01.2013 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka in Title Suit No.34 of 2011 is hereby affirmed.
